subject: Unit-6 • Uttarakhand Current Affairs (Mana Village Avalanche Rescue Operation – February-March 2025)
question: On 28 February 2025, out of 54 workers buried under snow in a massive avalanche that hit the Border Roads Organization (BRO) camp near India's first village 'Mana' ahead of Badrinath Dham in Chamoli district, 46 workers were rescued alive in a 60-hour joint rescue operation by the Indian Army (Ibex Brigade), ITBP, Air Force and NDRF. By what name was this relief operation conducted by the Central Command of the Indian Army?
options: Operation Mana (Ibex Brigade Avalanche Rescue Operation)
verificationSource: Ministry of Defense (Surya Command Indian Army) and Uttarakhand Disaster Management Department (March 2025)
explanation: On February 28, 2025, a massive avalanche following heavy snowfall hit the container labor camp of the Border Roads Organization (BRO) located between Badrinath and Mana Pass at an altitude of 3,200 meters in Chamoli district, burying 54 workers. Panchshul/Ibex Brigade of the Indian Army, ITBP, Cheetah/MI-17 helicopters of the Air Force, NDRF and SDRF conducted a daring rescue operation of about 60 hours with the help of Recco radar and thermal imaging in sub-zero (-15°C) temperatures and safely evacuated 46 workers to Jyotirmath (Joshimath) Military Hospital (8 workers died tragically).

subject: Unit-6 • Uttarakhand Current Affairs (Change in cultural names of tehsils and cities - March 2025)
question: In March 2025, the Uttarakhand government announced the change of names of more than 15 places/gram panchayats/towns in Haridwar, Dehradun, Nainital and Udham Singh Nagar districts in accordance with public sentiments and Indian cultural heritage. In this context, what mythological name has been given to 'Joshimath' tehsil of Chamoli district earlier (in 2024–25) with the approval of the Centre, and what has been renamed 'Kathgodam-Haldwani Marg (Nawabi Road)' of Nainital district and 'Aurangzebpur' of Haridwar respectively in March 2025?
options: The name of any of these places has not been changed
Name of Joshimath: 'Karnapur'; Name of Nawabi Road: 'Nehru Marg'; Name of Aurangzebpur: 'Akbar Nagar'
Name of Joshimath: 'Vishnunagar'; Name of Nawabi Road: 'Gandhi Path'; Name of Aurangzebpur: 'Lodipur'
Name of Joshimath: 'Jyotirmath'; Name of Nawabi Road (Haldwani): 'Atal Marg'; Name of Aurangzebpur (Haridwar): 'Shivaji Nagar'
verificationSource: Information and Public Relations Department Uttarakhand Government Notification (June 2024 and March 31, 2025)
explanation: The name of 'Joshimath' of Chamoli district, which was the penance of Adi Guru Shankaracharya, has been officially changed to 'Jyotirmath' with the approval of the Central Government and the name of 'Kosia Kutauli' tehsil of Nainital has been changed to 'Kainchi Dham' tehsil after the name of Baba Neeb Karori Maharaj's Dham. In this sequence, on March 31, 2025, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami announced the change of names of 15 places in Haridwar, Dehradun, Nainital and Udham Singh Nagar, in which 'Aurangzebpur' of Haridwar will be renamed as 'Shivaji Nagar', 'Ghaziwali' will be renamed as 'Arya Nagar', 'Mianwala' of Dehradun will be renamed as 'Ramji Wala', Nainital (Haldwani) will be renamed as 'Nawabi Road' has been named 'Atal Marg' and 'Sultanpur Patti' Nagar Panchayat of Udham Singh Nagar has been named 'Kaushalya Puri'.

subject: Unit-6 • Uttarakhand Current Affairs (Dehradun-Delhi Expressway and Asia's Longest Wildlife Elevated Corridor 2025)
question: How many kilometers long between Mohand to Asharori (Dehradun) for the unhindered movement of wildlife (elephants and tigers) of Rajaji National Park and Shivalik Forest Division in the last section of the 210 km long 'Delhi-Dehradun Greenfield Access-Controlled Expressway' (NH-709B, which is reducing the travel time from 6.5 hours to 2.5 hours), headed for completion in the year 2025? 'Asia's Longest Wildlife Elevated Corridor' has been constructed?
options: 12 km long elevated wildlife corridor (and 340 m long black double-tube tunnel)
verificationSource: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (2025)
explanation: The fourth and final phase (Ganeshpur to Dehradun) of the 210 km long 'Delhi-Dehradun Expressway' costing more than ₹12,000 crore, connecting Delhi (Akshardham) to Dehradun via Baghpat-Shamli-Saharanpur, presents a wonderful example of the balance of ecology and development. To protect the wildlife in Rajaji Tiger Reserve and Shivalik Forest area, a 12 km long six-lane elevated wildlife corridor (which is the longest wildlife corridor in Asia) has been constructed on pillars over the forest and a 340 meter long 'Dat Kali Tunnel' has been constructed at the entrance of Dehradun.

subject: Unit-6 • Uttarakhand Current Affairs (Jamarani Dam Multipurpose Project and Song Dam Drinking Water Project 2025)
question: On which rivers are the much awaited 'Jamrani Dam Multipurpose Project' of Kumaon region included under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana - Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Program (PMKSY-AIBP) (cost ₹ 3,678 crore, whose construction work is going on at a fast pace in 2025) and 'Song Dam Project', which will provide gravity-based drinking water to Dehradun city by the year 2050, are being constructed respectively?
options: Jamrani Dam: Sharda River; Saung Dam: Bhagirathi River
Jamrani Dam: Kosi River; Saung Dam: Tons River
Jamrani Dam: Gaula River (Nainital); Saung Dam: Saung River (Dehradun-Tehri border)
Jamrani Dam: Saryu River; Saung Dam: Mandakini River
verificationSource: Irrigation Department, Government of Uttarakhand and Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India (2025)
explanation: The 'Jamrani Dam Project', considered the lifeline for the Bhabar-Terai region of Kumaon, is being constructed (150.6 meter high roller compacted concrete dam) on the 'Gola River', 10 km upstream of Kathgodam in Nainital district. With this, Haldwani city will get 117 MLD drinking water, irrigation of 1.5 lakh hectares of land in Nainital-Udham Singh Nagar and Rampur-Bareilly of UP and 14 MW electricity till the year 2055. For a permanent solution to the drinking water problem of Dehradun, a 130.6 meter high 'Saung Dam' (150 MLD gravity drinking water + 6 MW electricity) is being built on the 'Saung River', a tributary of Ganga.

subject: Unit-6 • Uttarakhand Current Affairs (Adi Kailash and Om Parvat Darshan and Heli Tourism 2025)
question: In the context of the journey to the holy 'Adi Kailash' (Chhota Kailash - Jyolingkang) and 'Om Parvat' (Nabhidhang) located in the Vyas Valley of Pithoragarh district, for the convenience of the pilgrims, the Uttarakhand Tourism Department is running the aerial darshan (Heli-Darshan) and all-terrain vehicle package service of Adi Kailash and Om Parvat from the year 2024-25 for the convenience of the pilgrims, from which border place, so that the tourists coming here Has the number of devotees increased manifold?
options: Pithoragarh (Naini Saini Airstrip) and Gunji (Beas Valley Base Camp)
verificationSource: Uttarakhand Tourism Development Council (UTDB) and Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam (KMVN) Release (2025)
explanation: After Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Parvati Kund (Jyollingkang — Adi Kailash) and Gunji in October 2023, the Vyas Valley of Pithoragarh has emerged as a major spiritual tourism hub of the country. Along with the construction of Tawaghat-Lipulekh road by BRO, Uttarakhand Tourism Development Council (UTDB) has started special 'Heli-Darshan Service' (MI-17 and Twin Engine Helicopter Package) to Adi Kailash, Parvati Sarovar and Om Parvat from 'Pithoragarh (Naini Saini Airport)' and 'Gunji', the main center of Vyas Valley, during winter and summer season. Besides, the master plan of 'Shiv Dham' is also being developed in Gunji.

subject: Unit-6 • Uttarakhand Current Affairs (Chief Minister Ekal Mahila Self-Employment Scheme and Higher Education Promotion - 2025)
question: Under the 'Mukhyamantri Ekal Mahila Self-Employment Scheme' approved by the Uttarakhand Cabinet on the occasion of International Women's Day in March 2025 to make the destitute, widowed, abandoned, divorced and unmarried single women of the state financially self-reliant, a provision has been made to give how much percent direct government subsidy (grant) on the self-employment project cost (up to a maximum of ₹ 2 lakh) to the eligible women?
options: 75 percent subsidy (direct grant up to maximum of ₹ 1.50 lakh and only 25% loan share)
Zero subsidy, loan at only 18% interest
verificationSource: Women Empowerment and Child Development Department, Uttarakhand Government and Cabinet Decision (March 2025)
explanation: In the Uttarakhand Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami in March 2025, 'Chief Minister Ekal Mahila Self-Employment Scheme' was approved to provide economic self-reliance to single women of the state (widows, abandoned, divorced, crime and acid attack victims and unmarried women aged 35 to 45 years). Under this scheme, 'direct subsidy of 75 percent (i.e. up to ₹ 1.50 lakh) will be given by the state government on the project cost up to ₹ 2 lakh for starting micro enterprises like agriculture, animal husbandry, boutique, beauty parlor, homestay, public service center etc., while the beneficiary will have to invest only 25% through low interest loan.
